source.title: CrystalREPA: Transferring Physical Priors from Universal MLIPs to Crystal Generative Models
source.authors: Chengqian Zhang; Yucheng Jin; Duo Zhang; Tiejun Li; Han Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study deliberately aligns crystal-generator representations to frozen MLIP representations as a training method for improving crystal generation. It does not test whether independently trained models naturally become more similar as they scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports generation-quality metrics and energy-prediction probing after its deliberately induced alignment. These do not measure convergence in pairwise distances between independently trained models. Its figures and tables on metastability, validity, and other generation outcomes are therefore not rows for the claim. It also reports representation-distinguishability metrics within individual MLIP teachers, not convergence between models.
record.test_reason: The study deliberately aligns crystal-generator hidden states to frozen MLIP representations with a contrastive loss (induced alignment) and reports generation quality and energy-probe MAE. It never measures natural similarity between independently trained models, so no version is tested. It builds on REPA-style alignment as a tool rather than testing convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report a representation gap between generators and MLIPs that alignment narrows, and improved stability, validity and fidelity across 3 generators, 10 teachers and 2 datasets. They find that teacher distinguishability (TRI, EnRI), not Matbench accuracy, predicts transfer effectiveness.
record.recipe_differences: The method uses a training-time, element-aware contrastive alignment objective with a learned projection head and paired atom representations; it does not reproduce a method for testing natural convergence across models.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported probe results concern the second encoder layer. The paper also reports that alignment outcomes vary with alignment layer, alignment weight, temperature, objective, and MLIP teacher, but these are settings of the deliberately trained method rather than tests of convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla crystal generators' representations are far less predictive of formation energy than MLIP representations. Induced alignment cuts probe MAE (e.g. CrystalFlow 0.338 to 0.158).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generative crystal models trained without energy supervision do not naturally share the energy-relevant representation structure of energy-supervised MLIPs, but training-time alignment can impose it.

record.problems: The study does not directly test the catalog claim's convergence behavior or pairwise-distance measure. The relevant energy-probing table gives no uncertainty values; the authors describe other generation results as averages over five independent sampling and evaluation runs.
record.rows_left_out: Generation metrics in Tables 1, 2, and 5–16 were left out because they report crystal-generation outcomes rather than representational convergence. Representation-distinguishability analyses were also left out because they assess individual teachers' atom-wise representations and their association with transfer performance, not similarity between independently trained models.

untested.parts: All: no measure of cross-model alignment versus scale or capability.
All: a learned projection head maps student to teacher, but it is trained jointly with the induced alignment. No mapping loss between independently trained models is reported.
All: no feature or circuit recurrence analysis.
All: no similarity-metric sensitivity analysis of convergence.
All: the data-overlap analysis (C.7) concerns transfer gains, not natural alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The 'representation gap' finding (vanilla generators less energy-predictive than MLIPs) is a probing-quality comparison, not a similarity measure between models, so it bears on no version. Teacher distinguishability indices are computed within single models.

versions.untested_parts: Whether independently trained models with differing architectures, objectives, data, or modalities become more aligned with scale and capability.
Cross-modal alignment of vision and language representations on paired images and captions as the models improve.
Whether different initialization seeds produce shared features or subspaces.
Whether independently trained models' representations can be mapped or stitched with little loss, or aligned without paired data.
Whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
Whether convergence findings depend on similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
Whether cross-model alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.
